messages:
david: Paging on-call — we're seeing a sustained throughput drop and p95 degration for the apac-inference pool starting ~06:12 UTC. Grafana shows a concurrent connection spike and GPU utilization on some nodes at 98%. Customers in APAC complaining about slow replies. tagging @lia for immediate.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED • id=INC-2026-3300 • severity=degraded-performance • routed to: oncall-sre • started_at=2026-03-15T06:15:11Z
maria: I can take lead on runbook. Quick check: is autoscaler healthy? alex, can you confirm pool size and any recent deploys in the last hour?
alex: no deploys in last hour. autoscaler shows cooldowns, one ASG hit instance limits. a few hosts are flapping due to OOM on worker 7.
lia: oncall here — I'm digging into the flapping nodes. preemptively pulling traffic off apac-gpu-7 and 8 to avoid cascading. Initiating graceful drain.
david: good. we should fail traffic to eu variants for APAC traffic while we clear the flapping nodes. low-impact roll for routing policy now.
ops-bot: PLAYBOOK ACTION • draining node apac-gpu-7 • command: ./infractl drain --node apac-gpu-7 --grace 60s
alex: node drain started. also increasing pool target by +3 where quotas allow.
maria: creating statuspage draft. Suggestions for phrasing? keep short and actionable.
david: include what customers will see, scope (APAC only), mitigations in motion, ETA (estimate), and link to support.
---
maria: STATUSPAGE DRAFT (paste below for review):

"We are currently experiencing degraded inference performance for a subset of customers routed through our APAC inference pool. Impact: increased response latency (p95 elevated) and transient failures for some requests. Mitigation: engineering is draining affected nodes, scaling capacity, and routing traffic to nearby regions where applicable. ETA: 30-45 minutes for recovery. We will post updates every 15 minutes. If you are experiencing severe impact, please contact support with your request id."

alex: Looks good. I'd add: "No model correctness impact observed." and a link to the customer-facing incident page once published.
maria: updated draft with that sentence.

sam-cs: Sending a customer-facing message template to reuse for affected accounts:

"Hi <CustomerName>,

We’re reaching out about a service disruption affecting inference performance for requests routed to APAC. You may see slower responses or intermittent timeouts for a limited subset of requests. Our engineers are actively mitigating the issue (draining affected hosts, scaling additional capacity, and routing traffic to nearby regions). We expect recovery within 30-45 minutes. We'll post updates at: https://status.redwood.ai/INC-2026-3300. If you see continued impact after that window, please reply to this message and include any example request IDs. Apologies for the disruption — we understand this impacts your users and are treating it with high priority. — Redwood Support"

lia: Thanks Sam. I'll paste that to top impacted customers once status page goes live. Oncall note: I've attached logs from node apac-gpu-7 showing repeated OOMs and long GC pauses.
david: mitigation plan summary for the thread: 1) drain the flapping nodes (in progress) 2) increase pool target +3 where quota allows (in progress) 3) reroute APAC traffic to EU fallback for latency-sensitive customers (in progress) 4) monitor queue lengths and KV cache hit rates 5) if recovery stalls, execute temporary rate limit for non-critical tiers
maria: ops, can we get an ETA estimate on when drained nodes will be back in rotation?
ops-bot: NODE MAINT • apac-gpu-7 • drained • health checks failing • reason: repeated OOM • suggested action: reprovision with larger instance profile or reprovision group. estimated 18-30 minutes to reprovision depending on capacity.
alex: reprovision started for two replacement hosts. I'll also bump quantization-friendly model variant for the affected pool to reduce mem pressure where possible.
lia: handoff note — I'm handing primary incident pager to @maria at 06:40 UTC for the next 2 hours while I run node reprovision. checklist for handoff: 
- confirm statuspage is published ✓
- ensure customer notifications queued ✓
- confirm routing fallback in place ✓
- keys: watch p95, error-rate, queue_length
maria: taking primary. I'll keep posting updates every 15 mins and ping infra if we hit reprovision delay.

---
30m UPDATE (maria):
- node drain completed for apac-gpu-7/8
- two replacement hosts are provisioning (approx ETA 12-20 mins)
- traffic routing policy applied for latency-sensitive customers -> now routed to EU variants
- overall token throughput recovered to ~85% of baseline, p95 improved from 1.3s -> ~760ms

Next steps: watch for full capacity return, remove temporary routing when p95 stable <500ms for 10m.

ACTION ITEM (for post-incident): collect OOM traces, evaluate memory tuning for model shard placement, consider increasing alert threshold for host OOM. assign to infra team.

maria: publishing status page now and sending customer-notify for top 15 affected accounts. posting RFC for follow-up remediation.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE • INC-2026-3300 • status=monitoring • updated_at=2026-03-15T06:45:31Z

alex: thanks team. Lia, DM me the reprovision logs when you have them and we'll run the postmortem runbook after stabilization. :thumbsup:

lia: will do. handing back monitoring to @maria — I'll be available as backup. Good job everyone. :heart:

-- end of thread --"
